q1.answer_given: The incoming ALN Act adds pressure to an already-stretched system; Torfaen schools are already behind on funding and making hard choices. PRU staff training funding is often overlooked relative to mainstream school staff, though government partly addressed this after being pushed. Delegation levels to schools are already very high and not the real exclusion driver — instead the narrow key-stage-4 attainment measure and rising ALN costs (with tribunal pressure seen in England) are bigger factors; local authorities are working with Estyn and the Welsh Government toward a broader range of measures to address this more constructively. ALN legislation also extends obligations up to age 25, adding pressure on the post-16 sector. Term-to-term and week-to-week variation in provision needs makes budgets hard to plan for, and funding only follows a child annually, creating a lag when learners move between school and EOTAS. Separately, on diagnosis vs. support, diagnosis alone has limited value without proper support behind it — up to 50% of a classroom could have an additional learning need, and what matters most is an inclusive school for every learner, diagnosed or not.
